title: Trace protection zones and the full trip chain
lead: Protection is not a green status field at one current. It is a chain from the actual fault through measurement, logic, DC supply and interruption. Use a declared inverse-time curve to learn how a calculation behaves, then inspect what that curve cannot establish about CT saturation, electrical zones or selectivity.
objectives: Evaluate the stated inverse-time teaching model.
Distinguish a nominal timing margin from full coordination.
Identify CT-defined zone boundaries and end-to-end trip evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate the model, not a product
sections.body: For current multiple M greater than 1, the declared curve is trip time = 0.14 × TMS / (M^0.02 − 1) seconds. M = 10 and TMS = 0.1 produce approximately 0.297 s; M = 5 and TMS = 0.2 produce approximately 0.856 s. The difference is about 0.559 s, but breaker interruption, tolerances, CT behaviour and other active functions still matter. As M approaches 1 from above, the model time increases sharply.

sections.title: Separate thermal and measurement screens
sections.body: The adiabatic conductor screen is area ≥ fault current × sqrt(clearing time) / k. At 20 kA, 0.2 s and illustrative k = 143, the area is approximately 62.55 mm² before other selection checks. A resistive CT burden model gives VA = secondary current² × loop resistance: at 2 Ω, 1 A gives 2 VA while 5 A gives 50 VA. Neither scalar screen establishes complete cable suitability or freedom from CT saturation.

sections.title: Draw the actual zone boundary
sections.body: Protection zones follow CT locations, conductors, breakers, trip matrices and backup logic. A length-overlap comparison alone cannot establish coverage. The manuscript’s workbook is explicitly a set of constructed examples, not approved operating settings. Incident energy also depends on the adopted model, geometry, source state, current and clearing behaviour. Do not replace missing evidence with a universal arc-flash threshold, clearance time or safety certificate.

challenge.question: What happens near the pickup boundary?
challenge.answer: The declared trip time rises to approximately 1.0029 s. At M ≤ 1 this equation is outside its finite trip domain; do not display a misleading zero-second trip.

instructions: Read the declared boundary and units. Predict the selected result before calculating.
Run the starting case and inspect the ledger, assumptions and model limits.
Apply the challenge, run again, and explain the difference. Export only the last completed inputs and results.

scene.title: CT-defined zones over a breaker cutaway
storyboard: Reveal CT1, CB1, CT2, cable, CT3 and CB2.
Overlay zone boundaries tied to the CT positions, not decorative distance bands.
Select a fault location and illuminate its documented detection/trip chain.
Expose missing coverage or degraded trip DC without producing a safety approval.
scene.interaction: Inspect fault locations with buttons as well as pointer selection; change M and TMS in a labelled teaching-curve view.
scene.staticAlternative: Zone-membership table, trip-matrix narrative and numerical curve values.
scene.projection: orthographic axonometric SVG with upright HTML labels
scene.timelineSemantics: Narrative steps unless an explicitly labelled physical-time model is active.
scene.reducedMotion: Same states and values; no particles, parallax, camera travel or tweening.

assessments.question: Evaluate the declared inverse curve at M = 2, TMS = 0.1.
assessments.rubric: Use the stated exponent and retain seconds.

assessments.question: Find the conductor screen for 10 kA, 0.5 s and k = 143.
assessments.rubric: Use amperes, seconds and the declared k units.

assessments.question: Describe a breaker outside both CT-defined protection zones.
assessments.answer: Show the uncovered conductor or breaker segment and identify the missing detection or backup tripping arrangement.
assessments.rubric: Electrical connectivity, not an overlap distance, controls the answer.

limits: No relay settings for real equipment, live-work guidance or incident-energy calculator.
Teaching curves must not be represented as a verified manufacturer implementation.
